verdict.summary: Creating a public connection and connecting your own account is quick and needs no review. The hard parts are the unrecorded Gate 2 behaviour (whether other workspaces can install before review) and the Marketplace listing review, whose criteria Notion does not publish in the pages I could read.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for your own connection through Composio; add 1-2 days to prepare listing materials if you want Marketplace listing
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 30-60 min once the Client ID and Secret are in Composio, provided the token exchange succeeds
verdict.approval_wait: None documented for creating and using a public connection. Marketplace listing: Notion says to expect a reply within 5-10 business days.

gates.name: Public connection, your own workspace
gates.unlocks: Create the connection, get Client ID and Secret, and connect your own Notion account through Composio or your own redirect.
limits: Installation scope is fixed at creation; changing it means creating a new connection (f5).
Internal connections are the default in some guidance; the connection must be set to Public to get a Client ID, Secret and redirect URI (f7).

gates.name: Public connection, not listed (invited/other workspaces)
gates.unlocks: Other Notion users can authorize the connection through its OAuth flow without a Marketplace listing. Each user authorizes individually and gets their own token.
limits: No user cap or install cap is stated in the docs I read (f40).
Per-connection limit: 180 requests/min on plans other than Business and Enterprise (600/min on those plans) (f30).
Per-workspace limit is shared across all of a workspace's connections, so a connection can be throttled within its own budget (f31).
Data source queries: about 3 requests/second per connection; over-limit returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After (f32).
Free workspace block limit applies from September 8, 2026 and blocks API writes past the limit (f33).
Token endpoint can return 403 test_env_error; meaning not explained in the spec (f34).
The authorization URL is shown only after the connection is submitted for review, so whether unreviewed installs work is unconfirmed (f12).
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1, once the authorization URL is confirmed to work for an unreviewed connection

gates.name: Marketplace listing (Notion security review)
gates.unlocks: Your connection can be listed in the Notion Marketplace / integration gallery for discovery. Listing is optional; the OAuth flow works without it.
limits: Only public connections with installation scope 'Any workspace' are eligible; Internal and 'Selected workspaces only' are not (f23).
Public connections must pass a Notion security review before listing; the review criteria were not found (f21).
Notion reviews every listing; rejections cite brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, or unmet baseline criteria (f25, f27).
gates.time_to_reach: 5-10 business days after submission per Notion, plus any revision cycles

steps.title: Open the Notion developer portal and sign in
steps.detail: Go to app.notion.com/developers/connections and log in with the Notion account that will own the connection. The old notion.so/my-integrations link redirects to this page.
gotchas: The portal is JavaScript-rendered; if the page looks empty, reload after login.

steps.title: Create a new public connection
steps.detail: Go to Build > Public connections, click Create new connection, and fill in the connection name and development workspace. Set the connection type to Public, not Internal.

values.label: Connection name
values.value: Your app name (shown on the consent screen)

gotchas: New connections can default to Internal, which hides the client ID, secret and redirect URI fields.
Internal connections require the creator to be a workspace owner (documented for internal connections).

steps.title: Choose the installation scope
steps.detail: Pick the installation scope when you create the connection. It cannot be changed later; to change it you must create a new connection. Choose 'Any workspace' only if you plan to list on the Marketplace.

values.label: Installation scope
values.value: Any workspace OR Selected workspaces only (decide now; permanent)

gotchas: 'Selected workspaces only' cannot be listed on the Marketplace.
Switching scope later means a new connection and new Client ID/Secret.

steps.title: Set capabilities
steps.detail: Select the capabilities the connection needs, such as read content, update content, insert content, and read comments. Capabilities cap what any token from this connection can do, so enable only what your agent needs.

values.label: Capabilities
values.value: Read content, update content, insert content, read comments (as needed)

gotchas: Capabilities are set at creation; check the Configuration tab before inviting users.

steps.title: Enter the Redirect URI
steps.detail: In the connection's redirect URI field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. The value must include a protocol, with no fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or public IP address. Confirm the exact URL in the Composio dashboard first; Composio's docs list two different defaults.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Notion requires redirect_uri in the token request when more than one is configured or when it was sent in the authorization URL.
Composio's toolkit record and its guide list different default callbacks; use the one shown in your dashboard.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab of the connection and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret in a password manager; do not put it in source control.
gotchas: Both values are needed for the token exchange; a wrong pair returns invalid_client (HTTP 401).

steps.title: Enable your own developer authentication in Composio
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, open the Notion auth config, turn on 'Use your own developer authentication', and enter the Client ID and Client Secret from the Configuration tab. Confirm the callback shown matches the Redirect URI you entered in Notion.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list for Notion is empty; this is expected because Notion grants access per page on the consent screen.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Using Composio or the authorization URL, connect your own Notion account, pick a test page on the consent screen, and confirm the token exchange succeeds. Check the connection shows the pages you selected.

values.label: Authorization URL
values.value: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize (client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, state optional)

values.label: Token endpoint
values.value: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token (HTTP Basic CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET; JSON body grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri; Notion-Version 2026-03-11)

gotchas: The authorization URL field in the portal fills in only after submission for review; if you cannot see it, test through Composio and record what happens.
The authorize step does not reject a bad client_id; errors show at the token exchange (invalid_client, 401).

steps.title: Check workspace plan and rate limits before testing writes
steps.detail: Confirm the target workspace is not on the Free plan past its block limit, since API writes are blocked past that limit from September 8, 2026. Plan for per-connection limits of 180 requests/minute (600 on Business/Enterprise) and about 3 data source queries per second.
gotchas: A per-workspace limit is shared across all connections in the workspace, so one connection can be throttled by others.
Handle HTTP 429 with the Retry-After header.

steps.title: Invite or install into a test workspace
steps.detail: Authorize the connection from a second Notion workspace (or a second user in the same workspace) to confirm it works for users other than the owner. Each user authorizes individually and gets their own token.

values.label: Installation scope tested
values.value: Selected workspaces only, or Any workspace, as chosen in step 3

gotchas: Whether other workspaces can install before review is not confirmed by the docs. If the flow is blocked, record the exact message and stop before listing.
A 403 with test_env_error may appear; its meaning is not documented.

steps.title: Verify token lifetime and refresh behaviour
steps.detail: Store the refresh_token from the token response. Call the refresh flow and confirm you receive a new access token and a new refresh token, and that the old refresh token is replaced. Handle the case where refresh_token is null or absent.
gotchas: Community guidance says access tokens never expire; official docs describe refresh. Verify with a live exchange before relying on either.
The response schema types refresh_token as string or null.

steps.title: Draft the public-listing materials
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy, terms of use, support email, company name and website, tagline, description, category and tags, logo and listing images. Keep copy plain; avoid marketing claims. Only do this if you plan to list on the Marketplace.

values.label: Required by listing
values.value: Name, description, category and tags, listing images and logo, public connection to associate

gotchas: Privacy policy, terms and support email requirements come from community guidance, not Notion's official listing page.
Company name and website appear in an Organization Information section per community guidance.

steps.title: Read the Notion Connection Gallery Best Practices and check the security review
steps.detail: Open Notion's Connection Gallery Best Practices guide and note any review criteria. Notion's security review requirements were not found in the pages I could read, so confirm them in the Developer portal before submitting.
gotchas: The best-practices page exists but was not accessible during research.

steps.title: Submit the listing in the Listings section
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, open the Listings section, create a draft listing, associate the public connection (installation scope must be 'Any workspace'), attach listing details and images, then submit it for review.
gotchas: If the connection is 'Selected workspaces only', it cannot be listed; you must create a new 'Any workspace' connection.

steps.title: Wait for review and check status
steps.detail: Notion says to expect an email within 5-10 business days. Check status on the Listings > Connections page; the listing moves to a Submitted section while under review.
gotchas: Your own OAuth flow keeps working during review; only Marketplace visibility is affected.

steps.title: Revise and resubmit if rejected
steps.detail: If Notion sends feedback or rejects the listing, fix the cited issues (brand, trademark, quality, or baseline criteria) and resubmit from the Listings section.
gotchas: Rejection reasons include brand/trademark issues and quality concerns; check the best practices guide before resubmitting.

requirements.detail: The connection must be created as Public to get Client ID, Secret and redirect URI fields.
Must include a protocol; no fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or public IP addresses. Use the Composio callback URL shown in your dashboard.

requirements.item: Workspace owner to create internal connection
requirements.detail: Documented as required for internal connections; public connection requirement is not described in the docs I read.
'Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only'; cannot change after creation.

requirements.item: Privacy policy, terms of use, support email
requirements.detail: Community guidance lists these for a public integration. Confirm against Notion's listing requirements.
Community guidance: enter in the Organization Information section when making the integration public.
Name, description, category and tags, listing images and logo, and the associated public connection.
Required before Marketplace listing. Criteria not published in pages I could read.
Internal and Selected-workspaces connections cannot be listed.

scopes.effect: Notion grants access per page on the consent screen. Composio's default scope list for Notion is empty for this reason; no scope request changes setup or review.

scopes.scope: Capabilities (read content, update content, insert content, read comments, etc.)
scopes.effect: Set at connection creation. They cap what the connection can do, and changing them after creation is not documented; enable only what the agent needs.

scopes.scope: Installation scope (Any workspace / Selected workspaces only)
scopes.effect: Fixed at creation. 'Any workspace' is the only option eligible for Marketplace listing and triggers the security review path.

blockers.symptom: New connection shows no Client ID, secret or redirect URI fields
blockers.cause: Connection was created as Internal, which is the default in some guidance.
blockers.fix: Create a new connection and set it to Public. Installation scope is permanent, so choose it again at creation.

blockers.cause: Client ID or secret does not match the connection, or the wrong connection was used.
blockers.fix: Recopy the Client ID and Secret from the Configuration tab of the same connection and update Composio. The authorize step does not reject a bad client_id, so the error appears only at the token exchange.

blockers.symptom: API writes fail with a workspace block-limit error
blockers.cause: The Free workspace limit took effect on September 8, 2026, and blocks API writes past the limit. This date is already past.
blockers.fix: Test writes in a workspace under its limit or upgrade the plan. Confirm the current limit in Notion's request limits page before testing.

blockers.cause: Not explained in the spec. It may relate to test or development workspace restrictions; unconfirmed.
blockers.fix: Record the exact response and the workspace type, then contact Notion support if it blocks testing.

blockers.cause: Brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or baseline connection criteria not met.
blockers.fix: Read the Connection Gallery Best Practices guide, revise the listing, and resubmit from the Listings section.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed OAuth for prototyping; no setup needed. Move to your own Notion public connection when you need your own branding, your own redirect, or users outside Composio. To switch, turn on 'Use your own developer authentication' in the Notion auth config and register Composio's callback on your public connection. Confirm the exact callback in the Composio dashboard, because Composio's toolkit record and guide list different defaults.

open_questions: Whether other workspaces or users can authorize a public connection before Notion's review is approved. The authorization URL appears only after submission, and the docs do not say whether unreviewed installs work.
Notion's security review criteria (required documents, domain verification, demo video, questionnaire) were not found. Connection Gallery Best Practices was not accessible.

Token lifetime is unclear. Official docs describe refresh tokens, but the schema types refresh_token as string or null. Community sources say access tokens never expire. A live exchange is needed to confirm.
Meaning of the 403 test_env_error code is not documented; it may relate to test or development workspace restrictions.

Composio's default redirect URI is inconsistent between its toolkit record (/api/v1/auth-apps/add) and its guide (/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). Confirm in the Composio dashboard before registering.
No user cap, install cap or dev-mode limit for unreviewed public connections was found.
No official prerequisite on account type (free vs paid), org admin, or business verification for creating a public connection was found.
